summary: Testimonial collection you own: a public submit page, avatars resized safely on your server, a moderation queue where nothing goes public until you approve it, a wall page, and an embeddable widget that renders the wall into any site without an iframe. No third-party hosting a page about you.

stack.why: a submission is one INSERT; the wall is one SELECT
the one dependency worth taking: resize, strip EXIF, reject fakes

stack.choice: One small vanilla-JS file, no iframe
stack.why: inherits the host page's font and scopes its own styles
uploads need disk and the widget needs an HTTPS origin

prerequisites.name: Node.js 22 or newer
prerequisites.why: Everything in this build runs on it: the server, the scripts, the tests.
prerequisites.get: Download the LTS installer from nodejs.org, or install with your package manager (brew install node, or nvm install 22). Restart the terminal afterwards.

prerequisites.name: A terminal and a code editor
prerequisites.why: Every step below is a command you type or a file you edit.
prerequisites.get: VS Code (code.visualstudio.com), Cursor or Zed. Open a folder for the project and use the editor's built-in terminal.
prerequisites.verify: You can open a folder and run a command in its terminal

prerequisites.name: Git
prerequisites.why: History for your code, and the way most hosts deploy.
prerequisites.get: Install from git-scm.com or with your package manager, then run git init in the project folder once it exists.

prerequisites.name: The site you will embed the wall into
prerequisites.why: Phase 5 is tested by rendering the widget on a different origin.
prerequisites.get: Your existing site, or a blank HTML page served locally on another port.

prerequisites.name: A random salt for hashing IPs
prerequisites.why: For rate limiting without storing addresses.

prerequisites.name: A small always-on server (VPS)
prerequisites.why: This needs one process running all the time with a public address. Uploaded avatars need disk that persists, and the widget needs an HTTPS origin.
prerequisites.get: Hetzner Cloud (from about 4 EUR), DigitalOcean or Fly.io. Ubuntu 24.04, the smallest size. You need SSH access and a public IP. Only needed for the deploy phase; develop locally first.

prerequisites.name: A domain or subdomain
prerequisites.why: A public address you own, so links you share never break when a provider changes.
prerequisites.get: Register at Cloudflare Registrar, Porkbun or Namecheap, or use a subdomain of one you already own. You add one DNS record in the deploy phase.
prerequisites.cost: roughly $10 a year, or free on an existing domain

prerequisites.name: Caddy on the server
prerequisites.why: Automatic HTTPS in front of the Node process. Without TLS the browser features this relies on (and your visitors' trust) do not work.
prerequisites.get: On the VPS: follow the install steps at caddyserver.com/docs/install for Ubuntu. One Caddyfile with your domain and a reverse_proxy line is the whole config.
prerequisites.verify: caddy version prints a version on the server

env.name: PORT
env.where: Any free port; Caddy proxies to it.

env.name: UPLOAD_DIR
env.where: Where resized avatars are written. Back this up with the database.

env.name: MAX_UPLOAD_MB
env.where: Reject files over this before reading them fully.

env.name: SITE_URL
env.where: Public base URL for the widget script and JSON endpoint.

env.name: EMBED_ORIGINS
env.where: Comma-separated origins allowed to load the widget data.

env.name: ADMIN_USER
env.where: Any username for the basic-auth admin pages.

env.name: ADMIN_PASS
env.where: Generate one: openssl rand -base64 24. Never reuse a real password.

phases.title: Submission
phases.goal: Store submissions as unapproved, exactly as typed, escaped only on the way out.

steps.do: Create the project and the testimonials table
steps.detail: testimonials (id, name, role, company, avatar_path, rating 1-5, body, source_url, approved default false, created_at, approved_at, ip_hash). Build the approved flag now even though the wall arrives in Phase 4.
commands: mkdir praise && cd praise && git init && npm init -y && npm pkg set type=module

steps.detail: Name, role, company, rating, body. Cap body at 1500 characters, require rating 1-5, strip control characters. Store text as typed; escape at render time. Works with JavaScript disabled.

check: A submission stores one row with approved = 0
An over-length body is rejected with a readable message
A body containing <script> is stored verbatim and later renders as visible text
traps: Never sanitize on the way in. You will lose the ability to tell a real apostrophe from an attack. Escape on output, every time.

phases.title: Avatars
phases.goal: Uploads that cannot hurt you: sniffed, resized, stripped, capped.

steps.do: Accept an optional avatar and inspect the decoded header
steps.detail: sharp(buffer).metadata() throws on non-images; reject anything that is not a real image regardless of extension or declared type.

steps.do: Resize to 128px square WebP with a JPEG fallback, strip EXIF
steps.detail: sharp(...).resize(128, 128, { fit: 'cover' }).webp(). Write under a generated filename; never reuse the uploaded name.

steps.do: Cap the upload while streaming and set a pixel limit
steps.detail: Stop reading past MAX_UPLOAD_MB. sharp({ limitInputPixels }) so a decompression bomb cannot exhaust memory.

check: A 12 MP photo becomes a small square file
A renamed .txt is rejected
A 20 MB file is refused before being fully read
The stored file has no EXIF

phases.title: Moderation
phases.goal: Approve, reject, un-approve, delete, with files cleaned up.

steps.detail: Pending list with approve, reject and delete; approved list with un-approve; a raw view per row.

steps.do: Delete the avatar file when deleting a row

check: Approving makes a row eligible for the wall
Un-approving removes it immediately
Deleting leaves no file behind in UPLOAD_DIR

phases.title: Public wall
phases.goal: Approved testimonials only, responsive, with a designed empty state.

steps.detail: Masonry grid of approved rows: avatar, name, role, company, stars, body. Lazy-load avatars. Mobile-first, dark mode.

steps.do: Render an empty state when nothing is approved

check: The wall shows only approved rows
It reflows from 375px to 1440px
An unapproved submission is absent from the HTML source, not merely hidden with CSS

phases.title: Embeddable widget
phases.goal: One script tag renders the wall into any page with no iframe and no style leaks.

steps.do: Serve GET /api/wall.json with CORS for EMBED_ORIGINS

steps.detail: Finds a target div, fetches the JSON, renders cards with every text escaped on injection. Scope styles with a unique class prefix. Inherit the host font.

check: The widget renders on a different origin
It does not alter any host page style
A testimonial containing HTML displays as text in the embed

phases.title: Abuse controls and deploy
phases.goal: Spam turned away, backups covering both database and files, live.

steps.do: Add a honeypot, a minimum fill time and a per-IP limit of 3 per hour in SQLite
Add /healthz, systemd, Caddy and a backup covering data/ entirely

steps.detail: The embed snippet verbatim, the statement that nothing appears until approved, and the note that avatars live outside the database and must be backed up with it.

check: The honeypot silently discards while showing success
The fourth submission in an hour is refused
A restore from backup brings back both rows and images

phases.title: Operate it like a product
phases.goal: Only for the product path: get told about new submissions, keep the box safe, never lose an avatar.

steps.do: Email yourself on each new submission
steps.detail: SMTP credentials in .env (Fastmail, Postmark or any provider); fire-and-forget with a timeout so a mail outage never blocks a submission.

steps.do: Add an uptime check on /healthz and structured request logs
Nightly off-box backup of data/ and one restore drill
Firewall and unattended upgrades on the VPS

check: A new submission produces an email within a minute
Stopping the service triggers an alert
The restore drill brings back avatars as well as rows

product.outcome: A testimonial service for one or a few sites: moderated by default, embeddable anywhere, with uploads handled the safe way and backups that include the files.

architecture.swap: Any handler writing the same rows
Object storage behind the same write/read functions
Any UI; the flag is the contract
A React widget could replace embed.js against the same JSON

operations.backup: tar of data/ (database plus avatars) nightly, off the box, thirty days kept.
operations.restore: Extract into a fresh checkout, start, check the wall and one avatar.
operations.monitoring: Uptime on /healthz; a spike in pending rows is a spam wave.
operations.incident: Spam wave: tighten the rate limit, bulk-reject from admin. Compromised box: rebuild, restore data/, rotate ADMIN_PASS and SMTP credentials.

releaseGate: Unapproved content never appears in any public response, verified with a fixture
Upload rejection paths verified with a fake image and an oversize file
One restore drill including avatars performed and dated
Widget verified on a different origin without style leakage

notIncluded: In-browser video testimonials: permissions, encoding, storage and playback are genuinely hard and a real reason their price exists.
Importing reviews from G2, Capterra or Google.
after: A per-project mode so one server collects for several sites
Layout options (list, carousel) selected by a data attribute on the embed tag
